The user rejected smoke-tests/extensions/extension/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/smoketest/extensions/resources/ResourceInstrumentationModule.java, saying: "No, I want a real world test, not something synthetic like this". Use an actual Spring Boot 1.3.8.RELEASE executable JAR launched with java -jar on JDK 8 and the agent built from this PR under production ignore settings. Reuse the existing legacy fixture and smoke-test infrastructure where appropriate. Include a supported JDK-8-compatible Log4j2 2.17+ version and the ordinary OpenTelemetry API, with actual runtime dependency JARs packaged for the legacy Boot launcher. Preserve the manifest and actual application-loader checks so a modern launcher, exploded classpath, or wrong JDK cannot accidentally substitute for the affected runtime.

The application should create a real span through the ordinary OpenTelemetry API, make it current, and log a message using Log4j2. Verify that the actual log output contains that span's exact valid trace and span IDs through normal Log4j2 context-data lookup. Exercise the agent's existing production log4j-context-data-2.17 instrumentation and its real ContextDataProvider service discovery. Do not use a custom agent extension, injected dummy resource, manual ThreadContext/MDC population, fake SpanContext, direct calls to agent helpers, or application-bundled OpenTelemetry Log4j2 provider/service descriptors to make this pass. No Dubbo, RPC, external service, or telemetry backend is needed. Keep the fixture and assertion as small as the real behavior allows.

Remove the synthetic ResourceInstrumentationModule and injected-resource.txt introduced by this PR, replace the manual resource-lookup application/assertions, and remove this regression's dependence on the test extension JAR. Keep unrelated existing extension tests and modern Spring Boot coverage intact. Update directly related Gradle wiring, inputs, and test names so the new regression runs through the existing smoke tasks.

Keep exactly .allowClass("org.springframework.boot.loader.LaunchedURLClassLoader") next to the existing Spring Boot ignores in AdditionalLibraryIgnoredTypesConfigurer. Do not broaden the allow rule or add hierarchy inspection, precedence changes, listener-reset changes, reflection-based loader construction, or global test-default changes.

Prove red/green execution using a built agent. With only that exact allow rule temporarily removed, the new test must fail because real Log4j2 log correlation is missing. Restoring the allow rule must make the same test pass with the expected IDs in the log output. Restore all negative-test edits before committing. Keep production additional-library ignores enabled from process startup, never use the internal disable-ignores workaround. Run narrow formatting directly before behavior validation and report exact commands/results and any environment blocker. Do not wait for CI.

The Log4j2 mechanism is a candidate, not an already proven reproduction under this launcher. If it does not fail without the loader fix, investigate the actual lookup path and report that result instead of weakening the assertion, retaining a synthetic fallback, or claiming a regression has been demonstrated. Do not silently substitute a different library.

replies.body: Implemented in `13b3e301`. The targeted smoke test passed with the allow rule restored and confirmed the exact valid trace/span IDs in Log4j output. Temporarily removing only that rule made the same test fail with valid expected IDs but blank Log4j context data; restoring the rule made it pass again.

replies.body: I couldn't satisfy all constraints together, so I reverted the attempted edits and left the branch unchanged. With `otel.traces.exporter=none`, the agent creates no span processor and `GlobalOpenTelemetry` returns a no-op span; the targeted test fails the retained valid-span guard. An app-local SDK plus a no-op processor creates valid IDs, but the real Log4j2 provider logs blank IDs, so it does not preserve correlation. The only in-agent route I found is `otel.javaagent.debug=true`, which installs `LoggingSpanExporter` despite the `none` setting. Would you prefer keeping `otel.traces.exporter=logging` for this regression, or allowing debug span logging while the configured exporter remains `none`? Separately, the targeted Gradle invocation also reports the fixture `jar` task's pre-existing configuration-cache serialization error.

threads.body: I think we should consider whether we could get rid of the library ignores. As far as I understand the problematic part is matching class hierarchies. In most cases we can efficiently match the class hierarchy by ensuring that super types are loaded before subtypes. This lets us avoid parsing the bytes for supertypes as we can look at the already loaded class instead. This strategy doesn't work with ibm class data sharing as there we don't have access to the bytecode when the class is defined an can't preload the supertypes. Idk, maybe we could come up with some instrumentation that turns off the class data sharing. Another case where the ignores could help is with non-name based matchers e.g. ones that apply when class has a method with an annotation. There I guess the ignores might also help reduce the time spent parsing classes.
